html:
Devil's Island is a small island off the coast of French Guiana, the most famous part of the French penal colony there, which received convicts from 1852 to 1953.

France sent about 70,000 prisoners to the penal colony, hoping they would settle the land after their sentences. Most died of disease, hunger and violence. The camps spread from the Îles du Salut to Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni on the mainland. Devil's Island itself held political prisoners, most famously Captain Alfred Dreyfus, wrongly convicted of spying, from 1895 to 1899.

Accounts of escapes, such as Papillon, made the name a byword for cruelty. France stopped sending convicts in 1938, and the last returned home in 1953. The Îles du Salut now lie under the launch paths of the space centre of French Guiana.
sum: Devil's Island is a small island off the coast of French Guiana, the most famous part of the French penal colony there, which received convicts from 1852 to 1953.
